newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling ends week firm against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling ends week firm against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling closed the week firm against the dollar on Friday on dollar inflows from foreign investors and agricultural exporters, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 54.80 to the dollar, compared to 55.49 on Wednesday.
It was posted at a mean rate of 89.01 shillings to the pound sterling, from 90.57.
"The shilling is strengthening quickly. Everyone wants to square off for the weekend," one dealer said.
Demand for the dollar waned after the shilling hit the 56 offer rate, leaving the market unmatched as selling interest from exporters and offshore banks revived, the dealers said.
After the public holiday on Thursday, trading on Friday was thin and would not fully pick up till next week, they added.
The money market was liquid, with overnight rates quoted at between six and 13 percent compared to between 10 and 13 percent on Wednesday.
